claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons exhibit a broad magnetocaloric response.
These as-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit prominent magnetic hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain nanoscale grains, significant interfacial strain, and compositional gradients.
Interfacial strain and compositional inhomogeneity govern the low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis in these low-dimensional samples.
Interfacial strain and compositional fluctuations pin magnetic domain walls.
Interfacial strain and compositional fluctuations disrupt formation of a coherent magnetostructural transition.
Bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type material exhibits a cooperative magnetostructural transition.
Disruption of the coherent transition broadens the magnetocaloric entropy-change peak under low applied fields.
Domain-wall pinning and transition disruption increase magnetic hysteresis.
Reducing a magnetocaloric material to a nanocrystalline or low-dimensional state can lower its magnetocaloric response relative to its bulk form.
Annealing at approximately 400 degrees Celsius for one hour in an inert atmosphere will relieve interfacial strain in the films or nanoribbons.
The proposed annealing treatment will reduce compositional inhomogeneity.
Annealing-induced strain relief will enable more uniform magnetic ordering and more cooperative magnetic-domain reorientation.
Annealed samples will have a narrower and higher magnetic entropy-change peak than the as-deposited controls.
Annealed samples will have lower hysteresis, coercivity-like behavior, and remanence than the as-deposited controls.
Processing or annealing state can alter the magnetocaloric entropy-change curve and refrigerant capacity of a high-entropy alloy.
The proposed mechanism should become less dominant as film dimensions increase and bulk-like behavior emerges.
Heat-transfer limitations can constrain the usable cycle frequency and alter the measured cooling response.
